data.body:
All 7 ACs implemented in worktree `impl-cb1b`. `make verify` running; nothing pushed yet.

**AC4 — the handle returns BEFORE the gate completes.** Parametrized over all three new
starters (`review_code_start`, `claim_ticket_start`, `transition_ticket_start`). The blocked
library op (`rebar.llm.review_code` / `rebar.claim` / `rebar.transition`) holds a
`threading.Event` for the whole scenario, so a start body that blocked on the gate could
never return; `anyio.fail_after(3)` makes that a deterministic failure instead of a hang,
and `elapsed < 2` plus a mid-run `gate_status(...) == "running"` assertion pins the
immediate return. A terminal-verdict-only test would pass against the blocking code that
caused this bug, which is why the AC called that out.

**AC5 — the invariant guard is non-vacuous.** Measured against the REAL `build_server()`,
not a hand-built subset: 67 tools, and all 5 of `review_plan` / `verify_completion` /
`review_code` / `claim_ticket` / `transition_ticket` now have both a base tool and a
`*_start`. Before this change only 2 did, so the guard would have failed on 3. A second test
keeps the hand-maintained roster honest by cross-checking the billable LLM gate tools
against it; `scan_spec` is excluded with a stated reason (billable, but not one of the three
gates, so cb1b's invariant does not reach it).

**AC7 — dedup.** Parametrized per starter: a second start fired while the first is provably
still blocked inside the op returns the SAME `job_id`, and the op ran exactly once. That is
the re-fire reflex this bug provokes, so it is the case that must not double-bill.

**Collision test for the AC2 decision.** `claim_ticket_start` fired against a live
`review_plan_start` for the same ticket gets a different `job_id` AND a different
`gate_type`, and the claim really runs rather than inheriting the review's `passed`. Without
the distinct `claim`/`transition` gate types this is a silent no-op claim — worse than the
timeout being fixed.

**AC6 — `docs/mcp-reference.md` is GENERATED, with a CI drift gate.** Hand-editing it would
have been reverted by the next regeneration. The real defect was upstream:
`scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` enumerates registrars explicitly and knew only 3, so the new
`register_ticket_async_tools` was invisible to it — the generated doc said 65 tools while
the server had 67. Folded the new registrar into the write-gated group (its starters are
write-gated mutations, so they belong beside the `claim_ticket`/`transition_ticket` they
front). Regenerated: 64 -> 67. `AGENTS.md`'s async-gate bullet, which named only
`review_plan`/`verify_completion`, now names all five starters, states that a gated claim
and a completion-verified close BOTH time out over MCP, and records that the ticket
starters apply their status change only when the gate passes.

**Tests:** `tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py` 37 passed. Targeted sweep
`-k "mcp or surface or docs or parity"`: 1018 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed — including the
generated-artifact drift gates that the doc regeneration had to satisfy.
